To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) we have identified 328 P RNAs from all published metgenomic sequences and (b) the phylogeny based on covariance model is better than the one based on the 16S rRNAs.
we have identified 328 new P RNAs from all published metatranscriptomic and metagenomic projects and that the J2/1 joint region is a distinctive feature of bacterial and archaeal P RNA.

we have found a total of 328 P RNAs from all published metgenomic projects, which are all Type A, and that the phylogenetic tree of P RNA from metagenomics data is in good agreement with the one based on the 16S rRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
deciphering RNA structural diversity from microbial metagenomics and offers a systematic phylogeny based on covariance model analysis of P RNA.
the systematic phylogeny based on the P RNA structure, which is the most conserved structure of all RNAs.
deciphering the structural and phylogenetic diversity of RNase P RNA genes from metagenomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the P RNA is a useful tool for phylogenetic analysis and that the metagenomic approach has been successfully employed to identify new P RNAs.
the metagenomic data are useful for discovering and analyzing RNA genes and that metagenomic data have the potential to be used as an alternative to traditional phylogenetic analysis.
P RNA genes can be systematically identified from metagenomic sequences and the phylogenetic relationship of P RNA genes from prokaryotic genomes can be inferred.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified 328 P RNA genes from metagenomic sequences, validated one of the archaeal P RNAts from Sargasso, and analyzed the RNA structural and phylogenetic diversity from the P RNA sequences.
we have identified and analyzed a new set of P RNAs from all published metagemonic sequences.

we have found and validated a large number of P RNA genes from metagenomic sequences, expanded by 60% our understanding of P RNA diversity in prokaryotes, and identified a number of P RNA features that are not present in 16S rRNAs, which would be of great value in future studies on RNA structural diversity and evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the P RNA is an ideal phylogenetic marker to systematically study microbial phylogeny and diversity.
metagenomics is a powerful tool for identifying new genes and their diversity, especially when the genes are noncoding and/or are not well annotated.
the RNA world is still alive and well, and the RNA genes are abundant in metagenomic sequences.
